title: Tram
statementMd:
The tram in Berland goes along a straight line from the point $0$ to the point $*s*$ and back, passing $1$ meter per $*t*_{1}$ seconds in both directions. It means that the tram is always in the state of uniform rectilinear motion, instantly turning around at points $*x* = 0$ and $*x* = *s*$.

Igor is at the point $*x*_{1}$. He should reach the point $*x*_{2}$. Igor passes $1$ meter per $*t*_{2}$ seconds.

Your task is to determine the minimum time Igor needs to get from the point $*x*_{1}$ to the point $*x*_{2}$, if it is known where the tram is and in what direction it goes at the moment Igor comes to the point $*x*_{1}$.

Igor can enter the tram unlimited number of times at any moment when his and the tram's positions coincide. It is **not obligatory** that points in which Igor enter and exit the tram are integers. Assume that any boarding and unboarding happens instantly. Igor can move arbitrary along the line (but not faster than $1$ meter per $*t*_{2}$ seconds). He can also stand at some point for some time.

## Input

The first line contains three integers $*s*$, $*x*_{1}$ and $*x*_{2}$ ($2 ≤ *s* ≤ 1000$, $0 ≤ *x*_{1}, *x*_{2} ≤ *s*$, $*x*_{1} ≠ *x*_{2}$) — the maximum coordinate of the point to which the tram goes, the point Igor is at, and the point he should come to.

The second line contains two integers $*t*_{1}$ and $*t*_{2}$ ($1 ≤ *t*_{1}, *t*_{2} ≤ 1000$) — the time in seconds in which the tram passes $1$ meter and the time in seconds in which Igor passes $1$ meter.

The third line contains two integers $*p*$ and $*d*$ ($1 ≤ *p* ≤ *s* - 1$, $*d*$ is either $1$ or ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a96155caca833b8e78612e472baac6dbdcf5eaaa.png)) — the position of the tram in the moment Igor came to the point $*x*_{1}$ and the direction of the tram at this moment. If ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ad5acd483f67f197ab7bb106f02b9d93b0d1f97a.png), the tram goes in the direction from the point $*s*$ to the point $0$. If $*d* = 1$, the tram goes in the direction from the point $0$ to the point $*s*$.

## Output

Print the minimum time in seconds which Igor needs to get from the point $*x*_{1}$ to the point $*x*_{2}$.

## Note

In the first example it is profitable for Igor to go by foot and not to wait the tram. Thus, he has to pass $2$ meters and it takes $8$ seconds in total, because he passes $1$ meter per $4$ seconds.

In the second example Igor can, for example, go towards the point $*x*_{2}$ and get to the point $1$ in $6$ seconds (because he has to pass $3$ meters, but he passes $1$ meters per $2$ seconds). At that moment the tram will be at the point $1$, so Igor can enter the tram and pass $1$ meter in $1$ second. Thus, Igor will reach the point $*x*_{2}$ in $7$ seconds in total.
statementZhMd:
伯兰德的电车沿直线在点 $0$ 和点 $*s*$ 之间往返运行，在两个方向上均每经过 $1$ 米需要 $*t*_{1}$ 秒。这意味着电车始终做匀速直线运动，并在 $*x* = 0$ 和 $*x* = *s*$ 处瞬间调头。

伊戈尔位于点 $*x*_{1}$。他需要到达点 $*x*_{2}$。伊戈尔每经过 $1$ 米需要 $*t*_{2}$ 秒。

你的任务是确定伊戈尔从点 $*x*_{1}$ 到点 $*x*_{2}$ 所需的最短时间。已知在伊戈尔来到点 $*x*_{1}$ 的时刻，电车所在的位置及其行驶方向。

伊戈尔可以在任意时刻进入电车，进入条件是他与电车的位置重合；他可以不限次数地进入电车。伊戈尔进入和离开电车的位置**不一定**是整数。假设上下车均瞬间完成。伊戈尔可以沿直线任意移动（但速度不能超过每 $*t*_{2}$ 秒 $1$ 米）。他也可以在某个位置停留一段时间。

## 输入格式

第一行包含三个整数 $*s*$、$*x*_{1}$ 和 $*x*_{2}$（$2 ≤ *s* ≤ 1000$，$0 ≤ *x*_{1}, *x*_{2} ≤ *s*$，$*x*_{1} ≠ *x*_{2}$）——电车所能到达的最大坐标、伊戈尔所在的位置以及他需要到达的位置。

第二行包含两个整数 $*t*_{1}$ 和 $*t*_{2}$（$1 ≤ *t*_{1}, *t*_{2} ≤ 1000$）——电车经过 $1$ 米所需的时间，以及伊戈尔经过 $1$ 米所需的时间，单位均为秒。

第三行包含两个整数 $*p*$ 和 $*d*$（$1 ≤ *p* ≤ *s* - 1$，$*d*$ 为 $1$ 或 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/a96155caca833b8e78612e472baac6dbdcf5eaaa.png)）——伊戈尔来到点 $*x*_{1}$ 时，电车所在的位置及其行驶方向。若为 ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ad5acd483f67f197ab7bb106f02b9d93b0d1f97a.png)，电车沿从点 $*s*$ 到点 $0$ 的方向行驶；若 $*d* = 1$，电车沿从点 $0$ 到点 $*s*$ 的方向行驶。

## 输出格式

输出伊戈尔从点 $*x*_{1}$ 到点 $*x*_{2}$ 所需的最短时间，单位为秒。

## 说明

在第一个样例中，伊戈尔步行而不是等待电车更加划算。因此，他需要经过 $2$ 米，总共花费 $8$ 秒，因为他每经过 $1$ 米需要 $4$ 秒。

在第二个样例中，伊戈尔可以先朝点 $*x*_{2}$ 的方向前进，并在 $6$ 秒后到达点 $1$（因为他需要经过 $3$ 米，而他每经过 $1$ 米需要 $2$ 秒）。此时电车也位于点 $1$，因此伊戈尔可以进入电车，并在 $1$ 秒内经过 $1$ 米。这样，他总共将在 $7$ 秒后到达点 $*x*_{2}$。
